industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the counter-case the strongest it has been and named: the US ten-year is 4.83% (down 50 basis points in two months; Goldman Sachs, 20 to 26-Nov), 33 basis points from the sector rows' trigger (back to D under 4.5%), Oppenheimer's 2027 theme is 'beneficiaries of lower bond yields' and Bell (20-Nov) likes UK real estate and homebuilders; the table's Underweights led the week's rebound. Held at F because the yield fell as a safety bid inside a tightening of financial conditions (Mark Wilson: 100 to 150 basis points), European yields rose this week with ECB minutes leaning to hikes, and every property sector reads D or F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26). This is the first row I would lift if the ten-year goes through 4.5% on an easing read. No Pool name, no live holding.

sector.key: N.6. Real estate - developers and services
sector.why: Double Underweight, carried: the most leveraged and most cyclical end of property, financed at the margin in a week when AI-linked credit widened; the ten-year 4.83%, 33 basis points from the trigger. Relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior). No Pool name. Counter-case: land banks re-rate first when rates peak; back to D if the US ten-year falls under 4.5% on an easing read.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried, now on fresh evidence rather than the stale spread: France's forward-looking PMI fell to 46.2 to 46.8, near its record low, 'a deepening downturn' (S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov; Goldman Economics, 24-Nov), Pivotus calls it 'a disaster', Macron is considering a constitutional 'golden rule' if markets stay unstable in January with Le Pen leading the polls (Pivotus, 23-Nov), and Stehn (Goldman, 22-Nov) expects France to stagnate until its elections. The premium in basis points was unread for a fourth week, so last week's staleness rule (to D if unread again) is overtaken by the political and activity evidence, said plainly. 15 Pool stocks are French-listed, most of them global businesses. Counter-case: a top letter on a country whose listed companies earn mostly abroad, and the mid-2027 election is far away. To D when the premium is read under 120 basis points for a month with the PMI off its low; to C under 100.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
